title: Who shipped the most BESS cells and systems in H1 2026?
gist: Global BESS cell and system shipments nearly doubled in H1 2026, but the market is bifurcating: cell manufacturing stays highly concentrated among Chinese leaders like CATL even as it slowly de-concentrates, while system integration is fragmenting fast as Tesla loses share and low-barrier new entrants crowd the mid-tier.

insights.claim: Global BESS cell and system-level shipments both nearly doubled in H1 2026 versus H1 2025, driven by booming grid-scale and residential storage demand.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Near-doubling of both cell and system shipments confirms BESS remains one of the fastest-growing segments of battery demand, an anchor thesis for capacity and materials investment decisions.
insights.locator: opening paragraph

insights.claim: Benchmark BESS analyst Calvin Xu frames H1 2026 as a shift from pure scale expansion to stratified competition, with diverging concentration trends between cell manufacturing and system integration and intensified mid-tier competition.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: This framework tells investors to stop treating BESS as one undifferentiated growth story and instead separately underwrite cell-manufacturing concentration risk versus system-integration fragmentation risk.
insights.quote: Beyond the robust headline growth, the market is undergoing profound structural differentiation.
insights.locator: quote from Calvin Xu

insights.claim: Global BESS cell shipments exceeded 490GWh in H1 2026, nearly doubling year-on-year, per Benchmark's BESS Service.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sets the absolute scale of cell demand investors can use to size upstream cathode/anode material requirements.
insights.locator: Which companies shipped the most BESS cells?

insights.claim: The top 10 BESS cell vendors, all Chinese companies, captured 83.3% of total H1 2026 shipments, yet their combined share dipped 6.3 percentage points year-on-year, indicating gradual de-concentration even as Chinese dominance remains near-total.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Chinese cell-supply dominance is a structural chokepoint for non-Chinese BESS deployers; the 6.3pp erosion in top-10 concentration is an early signal of a slowly diversifying supplier base worth tracking.
insights.locator: The global top 10 cell vendors, all Chinese enterprises

insights.claim: CATL led BESS cell shipments in H1 2026 with a 22.0% market share, roughly flat versus 21.7% in H1 2025, even though its absolute shipment volume doubled year-on-year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: CATL is growing in line with the overall market rather than gaining share, meaning its BESS cell leadership is stable but not currently compounding relative to peers.
insights.locator: CATL led with a 22.0% market share

insights.claim: HiTHIUM ranked second in BESS cell shipments with a 10.2% market share and 63.5% year-on-year shipment growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: HiTHIUM's above-market growth rate signals it is taking share from slower-growing incumbents in the cell tier.
insights.locator: HiTHIUM ranked second place

insights.claim: EVE Energy took third place in BESS cell shipments with a 9% market share and 54.9% year-on-year growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Confirms EVE Energy as a consolidating top-three BESS cell supplier alongside CATL and HiTHIUM.
insights.locator: EVE Energy took the third place

insights.claim: BYD Energy Storage climbed from sixth to fourth place in BESS cell shipments, reaching a 6.7% market share with 83.3% year-on-year growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: BYD's jump of two ranking positions in a single half-year shows it is one of the fastest share-gainers in cell manufacturing, not just system integration.
insights.locator: BYD Energy Storage climbed from sixth last year to fourth

insights.claim: Cornex rose from seventh to fifth place in BESS cell shipments with a 6.5% share and 116% year-on-year shipment growth, the fastest growth rate among the established top-five cell vendors.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Cornex's outsized growth rate flags it as a rising Chinese cell supplier worth watching for further share gains.
insights.locator: Cornex rose from the seventh to fifth

insights.claim: Ganfeng Lithium re-entered the BESS cell top 10 with 250% year-on-year shipment growth, and Great Power also grew over 200% year-on-year, driven largely by demand for its residential storage cells.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A lithium raw-material producer (Ganfeng) re-entering the top-10 cell rankings signals continued vertical integration pressure in the battery supply chain; Great Power's residential-storage-led growth flags residential BESS as a distinct fast-growing sub-segment.
insights.locator: Ganfeng Lithium re-entered the top 10 league

insights.claim: Players outside the top 10 captured 16% of BESS cell shipments, up 6.3 percentage points year-on-year, as tier-2 suppliers such as Sunwoda, Gotion High-Tech, LG ES Vertech, Pengcheng Infinite and Samsung SDI gain traction with narrowing gaps between them.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A widening, more competitive tier-2 cell-supplier field increases buyer optionality and pricing leverage for BESS integrators sourcing cells outside the top 10.
insights.locator: Players outside the top 10 captured 16% of the market

insights.claim: Global BESS system shipments reached approximately 313GWh in H1 2026, a 93% year-on-year increase, with far lower supplier concentration than the cell manufacturing market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The structurally lower concentration in system integration versus cells implies a more contestable, lower-moat competitive environment for capital allocators evaluating integrator business models.
insights.locator: Which companies shipped the most BESS systems?

insights.claim: The top 10 BESS system integrators accounted for 60% of shipments in H1 2026, down 16.8 percentage points year-on-year, with Tesla the only non-Chinese company among them.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A 16.8pp drop in top-10 concentration in a single year signals rapid fragmentation in system integration; Tesla's status as the lone non-Chinese top-10 integrator highlights how thin non-Chinese exposure is in this segment.
insights.locator: The global top 10 system integrators accounted for 60%

insights.claim: BYD Energy Storage took the top spot in BESS system integration in H1 2026 with a 9.1% market share (roughly flat year-on-year), after shipments rose 96.6% year-on-year and it jumped from fifth place in H1 2025 to first.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: BYD leapfrogging four ranking positions in one year to become the top system integrator, while also gaining in cells, marks it as the standout share-gainer across the whole BESS value chain.
insights.locator: BYD Energy Storage maintained its leading position

insights.claim: Sungrow Power ranked second in BESS systems with an 8.8% market share, down 5.4 percentage points year-on-year, despite shipments growing 19.6% year-on-year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sungrow's share loss despite positive absolute growth shows the market is growing faster than the former leader, a sign of intensifying competitive pressure even on incumbents.
insights.locator: Sungrow Power ranked the second

insights.claim: CATL took third place in BESS systems with an 8% share, down 1.6 percentage points year-on-year, on 68.5% shipment growth.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: CATL now ranks in the top three of both cells and systems, underscoring its increasingly vertically integrated position across the BESS value chain.
insights.locator: CATL took the third place

insights.claim: Tesla fell out of the BESS system integrator top three for the first time, holding a 7.1% market share (down 5.2 percentage points year-on-year) even as its shipments grew 11.5% year-on-year; Tesla's CFO said full-year 2026 energy-storage deployments are still expected to exceed the 2025 figure.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Tesla's absolute BESS shipment growth masks a real competitive erosion story - its 5.2pp share loss and drop from the top three signal Chinese integrators are outgrowing it, a relevant read-through for Tesla's energy-storage segment narrative.
insights.locator: Tesla fell out of the top three for the first time

insights.claim: HyperStrong took fifth place in BESS systems with a 7% share (broadly unchanged year-on-year) on 83.3% shipment growth, and has set a management target of 70GWh of system shipments for 2026, more than double its 2025 volume.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: HyperStrong's stated 2026 target of more than doubling shipments is a concrete, checkable milestone for investors to track against actual delivery through the rest of the year.
insights.locator: HyperStrong secured the fifth place

insights.claim: Sigenergy entered the BESS system integrator top 10 for the first time, driven by strong momentum in overseas behind-the-meter markets and a giga-scale project agreement with Oman Electricity Transmission Company in Duqm, showing overseas expansion and large-project execution are now core drivers of system-integration rankings.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sigenergy's rise via a single giga-scale overseas project shows how quickly integrators can climb the rankings through large contract wins, a pattern worth monitoring for other C&I/residential players chasing similar overseas deals.
insights.locator: Sigenergy, a leading commercial and industrial

insights.claim: Players outside the top 10 captured 39.8% of BESS system shipments, up 16.8 percentage points year-on-year, reflecting low technical barriers to entry and new entrants arriving from the PV and electrical equipment sectors.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Low entry barriers mean system-integration margins and market share are structurally harder to defend than in cell manufacturing - a key risk factor for valuing pure-play system integrators.
insights.locator: Given the relatively low technical barriers

insights.claim: Competition is fierce among BESS system integrators ranked 10th to 15th, with a number of firms - including Fluence, Goldwind, Trina Storage, StarCharge and Robestec - clustered in the 4-5GWh shipment range.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The tight clustering of shipment volumes just outside the top 10 indicates any of these mid-tier names could move up or down the rankings quickly, useful for tracking emerging system-integration competitors.
insights.locator: A considerable number of firms registered shipments

insights.claim: Benchmark analyst Calvin Xu characterizes the global BESS market as having formed a clear three-tier structure - stable top-tier leaders, fast-growing second-tier vendors, and crowded mid-tier competitors - and expects sustained fragmentation and full-spectrum competition to be the industry's long-term trend.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: This three-tier framework gives investors a durable lens for classifying BESS names going forward: expect top-tier leaders to hold share, second-tier names to keep gaining, and mid-tier competition/margin pressure to persist structurally rather than resolve quickly.
insights.quote: The global energy storage market has now formed a clear three-tier pattern. Stable top-tier leaders, fast-growing second-tier vendors, and crowded mid-tier competitors.
insights.locator: closing quote from Calvin Xu
